objections.original_statement: Two representatives of one fiber define competing transition laws; their maximal total-variation distance is delta.
objections.supported_defect: No operation distribution, visibility of the chosen operation, or corresponding conditional kernel is fixed. For a fixed deterministic translation the representative laws are Dirac measures and their TV distance is binary. Averaging uniformly over all translations with the operation hidden instead makes the next state uniform for every starting point, hence gives zero defect for every partition. These two interpretations do not support the same proposed graded/destruction diagnostic. The finite O(N*K*t) table also does not certify arbitrarily many conditioned histories without a sufficient-state or compact-certificate argument.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Freeze the randomized transition kernel and observable operation label, the information conditioned on, and the scope of histories. Distinguish a per-operation defect from a mixture defect. Either give a finite sufficient-state bound or leave complete-history certification and its cost as a prerequisite.
objections.clearing_check: A paper audit must derive the fixed-operation and hidden-uniform-mixture boundaries under the declared definition, explain what happens when all translations are added, and show which statistic the matched partitions can actually vary.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: the variation of log C across an edge is bounded by the logarithm of its transport and saturation cost
objections.supported_defect: The mechanism correctly states only a transported algorithm/presentation upper envelope. It does not define a minimum over a transport-closed presentation class or a reverse inequality. A one-sided constructive envelope alone does not bound a two-sided variation of arbitrary native presentation costs; additive transport costs also need an explicit normalization before a logarithmic ratio follows.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: State a precise one-edge, one-sided cost inequality, or define C over a declared transport-closed class and state both directional inequalities. Include the dual/round-trip degree multiplier, inversion conditions on the subgroup and description growth. Keep the logarithmic modulus conditional until its actual inequality is supplied.
objections.clearing_check: Derive the one-edge inequality and its identity and round-trip boundary cases on formal supplied costs; verify that the two-sided statement, if retained, follows from the stated class and both maps.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: the second factorial moment counts pairs of distinct tuple-orbits with the same public sum
objections.supported_defect: A diagonal automorphism sends a tuple summing to R to one summing to phi(R), so a fixed nonzero-target fiber is generally not stable under the full action. The proposal does not say whether it quotients the target jointly, restricts to the target stabilizer, or counts representative-target incidences. Separately, distinct tuple orbits need not be independent relation rows; the cost input eta=independent-orbits/raw-tuples lacks that distinction.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Define the tuple-target incidence space and group action and derive stabilizer weights there. Use distinct-orbit yield for the certified quantity; reserve informative rank yield for a separately justified conditional probability or an additional certificate.
objections.clearing_check: For one formal target moved by an allowed automorphism, track the transformed tuple and target and show the statistic is representative independent. The duplicated-orbit control must leave distinct yield unchanged; an additional same-rank control must prevent promotion from distinctness to rank gain.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: The neighbor derives an asymptotic height budget from rank and regulator. This proposal replaces its isotropic volume approximation by successive minima plus reduction-collision multiplicity
objections.supported_defect: IDEA-20260807-6533fd already describes CM anisotropy, a finite-height effective-rank knee, and counts of distinct reduction images by height. Calling its approach simply an isotropic volume approximation overstates what was replaced. Tracking all successive minima can still be a distinct refinement; no outright duplicate is established.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Supersede the nearest-work comparison to acknowledge the inherited knee and reduction-image census. Identify the extra information in the full successive-minima profile and any new collision certificate beyond the predecessor's two-regime/effective-rank model.
objections.clearing_check: Provide one matched abstract-lattice comparison with equal rank, determinant and predecessor classification but different successive-minima profiles, or specify another observable distinction the predecessor does not retain.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: A triangle with product multiplier not equal to one cannot admit a globally path-independent section
objections.supported_defect: For group/vector fibers and multiplier transport, the zero section is invariant under every loop, including a nonidentity multiplier. The stated impossibility is therefore too broad. A full trivialization or a section through a prescribed nonzero point has a different obstruction, and quotienting ambiguities can also erase the loop class.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Define the desired interface as a full fiber trivialization or a section through a specified nonzero point. State the ambiguity quotient and require the loop's action/class to remain nontrivial on that marked object.
objections.clearing_check: The same triangle must distinguish the always-compatible zero section from a prescribed nonzero marking or full trivialization. State exactly which object is refused; do not use refusal of every section as the control.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: Track the graded module of elements killed by a power of the denominator. Its last occupied degree is a candidate explanation for a degree gap
objections.supported_defect: Denominator torsion can have positive-dimensional graded support and nonzero components in arbitrarily high degrees. Finite generation does not imply a last occupied degree. A finite saturation exponent, a finite-length module's highest degree, and a truncated degree profile are different quantities.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Specify the grading and a finite-length hypothesis that makes the last degree finite, or replace it with a bounded-degree profile or a saturation exponent and revise the predicted relation to computation degree accordingly.
objections.clearing_check: A paper domain audit must include both a positive-dimensional boundary module and a finite-length boundary module; the reported invariant must remain defined in each admitted case and any implication for degree cost must be separately stated.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: An exceptional relation-rate effect can survive identical generic monodromy only if the chosen factor base meets branch or collision strata with a different weight.
objections.supported_defect: Generic geometric monodromy does not by itself fix finite rational-fiber frequencies or an arbitrary sampler's distribution on the open locus. The same proposal explicitly allows a residual away from every named degeneracy and asks for point-count error, which conflicts with the first sentence's only-if assertion.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Replace the necessity assertion by a conjectural decomposition with an open-locus arithmetic/sampling residual, or add explicit hypotheses and a bound that force that residual to vanish or be negligible. Preserve the useful stratified accounting and its finite scope.
objections.clearing_check: State a control with identical geometric monodromy and equal named-stratum counts but differing open-locus fiber/sampling distributions; the revised statement must allow or quantitatively bound its residual.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: Matched null: bipartite incidence tables with identical row and column totals.
objections.supported_defect: With one row per curve and row total Z_D under the fixed normalization, fixing every row total fixes E[Z_D], E[Z_D^2] and the hit fraction. That null cannot contrast the declared concentration statistic. It can only test geometry beyond row multiplicities if another statistic is added.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Keep the degree-preserving shuffle as an incidence-bookkeeping control and add a matched-total-mass/control family that allows the curve row distribution to vary, with the measure and automorphism weights held fixed. Name a new statistic if degree-preserving geometry is also to be tested.
objections.clearing_check: Symbolically verify that the revised regular and concentrated tables have the matched first moment but different second moments/hit fractions, while the row-preserving shuffle leaves those quantities unchanged.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: All local weights one and independent marks recover factorial moment lambda squared.
objections.supported_defect: For a finite sum of independent Bernoulli marks with probabilities p_i and mean lambda, E[S(S-1)]=lambda^2-sum_i p_i^2. The exact lambda^2 identity belongs to a Poisson count; the finite Bernoulli-to-Poisson approximation needs its error bounded. A deterministic norm multiset also needs a declared random marking/form ensemble to interpret its expectations.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Replace the finite baseline by its correct Bernoulli identity and align the dependence normalization with it, or explicitly adopt a Poisson reference with an approximation error. Freeze the probability space, distinguishing deterministic norm entries, residue weights and random marks.
objections.clearing_check: Derive the first two derivatives of the finite product generating polynomial and retain the diagonal correction. Any Poisson normalization must include a bound on the omitted sum of squared probabilities.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: Represent a morphism by its source, target and transition isomorphisms under the field automorphisms, retaining the cocycle defect on overlaps.
objections.supported_defect: Valid descent cocycles for source and target certify object descent, but the supplied morphism must also commute with their Galois descent maps. The proposed necessary-and-sufficient field certificate and C_iso cost do not explicitly state or price this morphism compatibility equation. This is a specification gap; it does not refute a full descent theorem with that equation included.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: List object cocycle checks and the separate equivariance square for each supplied morphism. Include exact morphism-equality/representation costs in C_iso by definition or add a separate term. Otherwise limit the output to compatibility of object descent data.
objections.clearing_check: Hold valid source/target cocycles fixed and compare a morphism satisfying the square with one violating it. The latter must be rejected even though both endpoint cocycles vanish.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: O(k log p) group operations plus big-integer CRT for k supplied witnesses
objections.supported_defect: For a general composite point-order claim, an annihilation relation alone is insufficient to certify the asserted order; factor-specific nonzero checks must be included. O(k log p) is coherent if k counts the verified prime-order/factor components, but the proposal currently calls k supplied witnesses and also permits general divisors and lcm composition. Charging primality certificates separately does not define the number of group checks.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Define k as the total number of required prime-factor order checks, or restrict witness units to explicitly certified prime/prime-power components. If k instead counts points with arbitrary composite claimed orders, include their factor-check count and witness bytes in the bound.
objections.clearing_check: A symbolic cost audit with fixed raw point count and varying numbers of distinct certified prime factors must preserve the stated operation bound and reject an annihilation-only claim whose order divisor is unsupported.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

objections.original_statement: An algebraic identity proving that the union of base loci has empty intersection with the permitted domain gives a completeness certificate.
objections.supported_defect: Joint chart coverage requires no point to lie in every chart's base locus: the common intersection of base loci must miss the domain. Requiring their union to miss it instead requires every chart to be individually defined everywhere and contradicts the stated two-chart goal. The later proof obligation correctly says empty common base locus.
objections.smallest_additive_correction: Replace union by intersection/common base locus. Specify the admitted rational or geometric input domain and keep group-law correctness on defined charts as a separate obligation from coverage.
objections.clearing_check: Two complementary incomplete charts with nonempty individual base loci and empty common base locus must pass the joint coverage condition; a remaining common omitted identity component must fail.
objections.scope_limit: Proposal specification review only; the proposed check was not executed and no mathematical lane is closed.

red_team_report.counterexample_or_mutation: The report supplies formal boundary objections and proposed clearing controls, including zero sections under multiplier holonomy, finite Bernoulli diagonal correction, fixed row-total moment invariance, and intersection versus union for chart coverage. These are proposal-statement checks, not empirical counterexamples or executed experiments.
red_team_report.baseline_comparison: The proposals disclose generic square-root-order baselines where relevant and distinguish certificate verification from search. Specialized correspondence probability proposals retain their conditional baseline tiers. No row supplies a validated end-to-end improvement here, and no full time/memory/data Pareto frontier was independently audited. Certificate/interface proposals are compared to their named internal method, not promoted by comparing their verification time to a complete discrete-log solver.
heuristic_challenges: RT1: a coupling bound needs the specified conditional kernel uniformly over allowed histories.
RT8/RT9: concentration and dependence controls must actually vary the claimed finite statistic.
Slots 7, 15, 18 and 22 retain explicit open mixing, separator, sheaf-transfer and norm-dependence assumptions; no failure is inferred merely from their being conditional.

Across all 48, supplied-certificate verification costs do not include certificate discovery by default; the per-ID notes preserve unpriced construction as a prerequisite rather than an established saving.
